Calibrate retention indices from an n-alkane standard

Source: R/retention_index.R
calibrate_ri.Rd

Identify a homologous alkane series using diagnostic ions and fit a smooth, monotone retention-time calibration. The retention coordinate uses peak onset plus half a local narrow-peak duration, reducing the influence of tailing.

Usage

calibrate_ri(
  standard = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  carbon = 7:40,
  anchors = NULL,
  spar = NULL,
  control = list(),
  psf = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'RIcalibration'
predict(object, newdata, extrapolate = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'RIcalibration'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

standard

ANDI-MS CDF path, scan-by-mass matrix, or list with Y and time.

time

Increasing scan times in minutes for matrix input.

carbon

Permitted carbon numbers, default 7:40. The molecular ion must lie within the acquired mass range. Supply the known standard range when available.

anchors

Optional data frame with carbon and retention_time columns, supplying verified calibration coordinates directly. An optional narrow_width column supplies local small-peak durations for timing sample profiles.

spar

Smoothing-spline smoothing parameter; NULL selects it by GCV.

control

Named calibration controls, described below.

psf

Optional calibrated PSF from L0nmf::estimate_psf(), or a list with psf_kernels (one kernel per row), psf_offsets in minutes and psf_timepoints (or peak_timepoints) in minutes. Its local width at the chosen height fraction supplies the small-peak duration. A single kernel gives a constant duration. NULL estimates a narrow-width envelope from the detected standard peaks.

object

A fitted RIcalibration.

newdata

Retention coordinates in minutes.

extrapolate

Use linear continuation outside the calibration range. FALSE returns NA outside the range.

...

Additional method arguments.

x

An RIcalibration object.

Value

An RIcalibration object with accepted anchors, all candidate diagnostics, fitted spline, local narrow-peak widths and timing convention.

Details

For an alkane with c carbon atoms the nominal molecular ion is 14c+2. Its excess above the carbon-13 isotope contribution of the adjacent alkyl ion is used with the 43, 57, 71, 85, 99 and 113 fragment series. Candidate anchors must have a coherent saturated-hydrocarbon spectrum. A maximum-weight increasing carbon-number sequence removes duplicate maxima and inconsistent assignments. Solvent-range C6 is excluded by default.

Peak onset and duration use a relative-height fraction of 0.01 by default. A supplied calibrated PSF gives its local small-peak duration; otherwise a local lower envelope of standard peak durations estimates that duration. Both standards and sample profiles use t_star = onset + narrow_width/2. A smoothing spline maps t_star to 100c; a monotone cubic interpolation through its fitted anchor values prevents local reversals. Extrapolation is disabled by default in predict().

control accepts fraction, baseline_window (minutes), min_separation (minutes), min_relative, min_molecular_fraction, min_molecular_ratio, min_alkane_fraction and width_quantile. The returned anchor table includes the molecular-ion evidence and calibration residuals for inspection. Explicit anchors bypass automatic assignment and use their supplied timing.

References

van den Dool, H. and Kratz, P. D. (1963), J. Chromatogr. 11, 463–471, doi:10.1016/S0021-9673(01)80947-X. <https://webbook.nist.gov/chemistry/gc-ri/>

Examples

a <- data.frame(carbon=8:15, retention_time=c(3,4,5.2,6.7,8.5,10.6,13,15.7))
cal <- calibrate_ri(anchors=a)
predict(cal, c(5,10))
cal
